conventions.convention: Complex Hilbert-space inner products are linear in the first argument. Commutants are taken inside B(H), and a concrete von Neumann algebra is a unital star subalgebra satisfying M=M''. Choice is assumed.
Cyclic means closure of MΩ equals H; separating means xΩ=0 implies x=0. Faithfulness of the unit-vector functional is equivalent to separatingness, and cyclicity alone does not imply it.
For densely defined antilinear S, its linearization maps the conjugate Hilbert space to H, and S*=c_H^{-1} times the linearization's adjoint. Thus ⟨Sx,y⟩=⟨S*y,x⟩ on the declared domains.
Polar decomposition for a merely closable antilinear operator is asserted for its graph closure, not for the original operator.

Positive-functional normality means preservation of suprema of bounded increasing positive nets. The predual lemma proves this for positive quotient functionals; it does not state the converse characterization.
The defining-representation counterexample assumes n>1; the Hilbert–Schmidt representation uses ⟨X,Y⟩=Tr(Y*X) and a positive-definite trace-one density matrix.

load_bearing.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. A densely defined closable antilinear operator has a closed graph closure with polar decomposition. For a concrete von Neumann algebra M and a vector Ω cyclic and separating for M, S₀(xΩ)=x*Ω on MΩ is well defined, densely defined, antilinear, and closable.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a concrete von Neumann algebra M⊆B(H), Q=S₁(H)/M⊥ is Banach and the trace pairing Ψ:M→Q* is an isometric bijection. Its dual unit ball is weak-star compact. Every vector functional and every positive functional in Q preserves suprema of bounded increasing positive nets in M.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a densely defined closed linear A:H₁→H₂, T=A*A is positive self-adjoint; P=T^(1/2) has D(P)=D(A) and ‖Px‖=‖Ax‖. There is a unique partial isometry U with A=UP and ker U=ker A, having initial space (ker A)⊥ and final space closure of ran A.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Finite-rank operators are trace-norm dense in S₁(H). Every bounded linear functional Φ on S₁(H) has a unique representation Φ(T)=Tr(TX), X∈B(H), with ‖Φ‖=‖X‖.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. The strong-operator closure of a unital star subalgebra R⊆B(H) is R''. For a concrete von Neumann algebra M, Ω is cyclic for M exactly when it is separating for M'.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. A norm-bounded increasing positive net in a concrete von Neumann algebra has a least upper bound in its positive cone and converges strongly to that supremum.

alerts.finding: The Definition says of Q from lem-qsmx-von-neumann-predual: “its elements are the normal linear functionals”, then independently defines normal states by preservation of bounded increasing positive suprema. The cited lemma proves only that positive quotient functionals have this order-normality property; it does not prove that every order-normal positive functional belongs to Q. If the opening sentence asserts that identification, its converse needs an additional proved supplier. If it merely introduces terminology for Q, clarify that distinction from the independently given order definition. Hiai, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.02383, §1.3, printed p. 4, explicitly states the positive-functional equivalence, but that overview passage supplies no local proof. The other inspected modular consumers use vector or explicit trace-class functionals and do not require this converse.
